questions.question: What is the primary motivation for using Binary Neural Networks (BNNs) in deployment?
questions.choice_A: To reduce memory footprint and enable efficient bitwise operations that accelerate inference
questions.choice_B: To improve model interpretability via symbolic reasoning
questions.choice_C: To guarantee zero training loss through discrete optimization
questions.choice_D: To replace the need for normalization layers entirely

questions.question: In BinaryConnect, how are weights treated during training?
questions.choice_A: Weights are ternarized in the forward pass and stored as ternary values
questions.choice_B: Weights are binarized in the forward pass but updated in real-valued form
questions.choice_C: Weights remain real-valued in both forward and backward passes
questions.choice_D: Weights are quantized to 8-bit integers for both inference and training

questions.question: Which statement best characterizes the Straight-Through Estimator (STE) in the context of binarization?
questions.choice_A: It provides an unbiased gradient estimate for the sign function
questions.choice_B: It replaces the sign function with a smooth sigmoid during inference
questions.choice_C: It passes gradients through a non-differentiable quantizer by using a proxy derivative
questions.choice_D: It calculates exact subgradients of the quantization operator

questions.question: What key innovation did XNOR-Net introduce for improving accuracy in BNNs?
questions.choice_A: Replacing batch normalization with group normalization
questions.choice_B: Using learned soft quantization with Gumbel-Softmax
questions.choice_C: Applying stochastic rounding to both weights and activations
questions.choice_D: Using scaling factors to better approximate real-valued convolutions with binary weights and activations

questions.question: Why might ternary weight networks (with values in {-1, 0, +1}) achieve higher accuracy than purely binary ones?
questions.choice_A: The zero state enables structured sparsity and a closer approximation to real-valued weights
questions.choice_B: They eliminate the need for STE during training
questions.choice_C: They avoid any quantization error by design
questions.choice_D: They allow exact inference on analog neuromorphic hardware

questions.question: What is the main difference between Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) and training a low-bit network from scratch without awareness?
questions.choice_A: QAT uses higher learning rates to counter gradient mismatch
questions.choice_B: QAT simulates quantization effects during training to align the learned model with its quantized inference behavior
questions.choice_C: QAT eliminates the need for backpropagation
questions.choice_D: QAT only quantizes activations, not weights

questions.question: Which consequence is commonly associated with binarizing activations in addition to weights?
questions.choice_A: Backpropagation becomes exact due to linearity
questions.choice_B: The model no longer benefits from batch normalization
questions.choice_C: Information loss increases, often requiring architectural or training adjustments to recover accuracy
questions.choice_D: The number of parameters must increase to maintain memory bandwidth

questions.question: Channel-wise scaling in BNNs typically provides what benefit over layer-wise scaling?
questions.choice_A: It reduces the number of scaling parameters to a single scalar per network
questions.choice_B: It guarantees hardware latency reduction under all workloads
questions.choice_C: It enforces identical distributions across channels, easing calibration
questions.choice_D: It captures per-channel magnitude differences, improving the approximation of full-precision weights

questions.question: What is the role of the abs-mean (mean absolute value) scaling factor in binarized layers?
questions.choice_A: To rescale binary weights so their expected magnitude better matches the underlying real-valued weights
questions.choice_B: To normalize activations to zero-mean and unit variance
questions.choice_C: To replace batch normalization during training
questions.choice_D: To stochastically sample quantization thresholds

questions.question: Which training trick is commonly used to stabilize BNN training?
questions.choice_A: Removing all normalization layers
questions.choice_B: Clipping or constraining the latent real-valued weights before binarization
questions.choice_C: Replacing ReLU with linear activations everywhere
questions.choice_D: Using dropout with extremely high rates (e.g., 0.9)

questions.question: In Ternary Weight Networks (TWN), how are weights typically mapped to {-1, 0, +1}?
questions.choice_A: Via sign only, without thresholds
questions.choice_B: By uniform quantization with evenly spaced codebooks
questions.choice_C: By applying a threshold to create zeros and using a scaling factor for non-zero weights
questions.choice_D: By learning a separate ternary classifier per weight

questions.question: What is a common limitation of the vanilla STE when used with the sign function?
questions.choice_A: It yields gradients that are too large outside the quantizer’s saturation region
questions.choice_B: It prevents convergence on convex losses
questions.choice_C: It causes gradients to be exactly zero in the linear region
questions.choice_D: It forces the use of second-order optimizers

questions.question: Why are real-valued accumulators often retained in BNN inference, even when weights and activations are binary?
questions.choice_A: Accumulation precision helps reduce numerical error in dot products before thresholding or scaling
questions.choice_B: Binary accumulators are not compatible with GPUs
questions.choice_C: Real-valued accumulators eliminate the need for scaling factors
questions.choice_D: This is necessary only for training, not inference

questions.question: Knowledge distillation is sometimes used when training low-bit networks because:
questions.choice_A: A teacher network can provide softer targets that guide the quantized student toward better decision boundaries
questions.choice_B: It removes the need for data augmentation entirely
questions.choice_C: It guarantees the student will outperform the teacher
questions.choice_D: It allows training to proceed without backpropagation

questions.question: Which statement best describes gradient mismatch in low-bit training?
questions.choice_A: The gradients are computed exactly with respect to the discrete parameters
questions.choice_B: The forward pass uses quantized variables but the backward pass uses surrogate gradients that do not match the true derivatives
questions.choice_C: The optimizer maintains separate gradient buffers for each bit
questions.choice_D: The mismatch refers to the difference between training and validation accuracy

questions.question: What is a key computational benefit of binarizing both weights and activations in convolutional layers?
questions.choice_A: It allows use of integer fused multiply-add units
questions.choice_B: It enables replacing multiplications with XNOR and bitcount operations
questions.choice_C: It replaces convolutions with FFTs automatically
questions.choice_D: It removes the need for caching intermediate activations

questions.question: How does quantization-aware training typically handle batch normalization in low-bit networks?
questions.choice_A: It removes batch normalization layers during training and inference
questions.choice_B: It folds batch normalization parameters into preceding convolutions and may quantize them consistently
questions.choice_C: It freezes batch normalization statistics at random
questions.choice_D: It replaces batch normalization with dropout to match quantization noise

questions.question: What is a common reason to prefer per-channel (or per-filter) scaling over a single layer-wise scale in convolutional BNNs?
questions.choice_A: Per-channel scaling simplifies compiler passes
questions.choice_B: Filter responses have different magnitudes, and per-channel scaling preserves relative energy across channels
questions.choice_C: Layer-wise scaling cannot be implemented on hardware
questions.choice_D: Per-channel scaling removes the need for activation quantization

questions.question: Compared to binary networks, what additional property can ternary networks exploit for efficiency?
questions.choice_A: Structured sparsity from zeros, enabling potential skip operations or sparse storage
questions.choice_B: Exact arithmetic equivalence to floating-point
questions.choice_C: Deterministic convergence in fewer epochs
questions.choice_D: Elimination of any need for scaling factors

questions.question: Which practical guideline is often followed when designing BNNs for accuracy on large-scale tasks?
questions.choice_A: Keep the first and last layers at higher precision while binarizing intermediate layers
questions.choice_B: Use no residual connections to avoid quantization noise propagation
questions.choice_C: Always remove data augmentation to avoid overfitting the quantizer
questions.choice_D: Use only layer-wise scaling to reduce parameters
